description: We make a wood-plastic composite siding board. Builders want to use it on walls close to the property line on small apartment buildings, where the code calls for noncombustible cladding. We have cone calorimeter results and a flame-spread rating of 75 but we have not done the full-scale exterior wall fire test. What do we need to get it accepted in Alberta?
known_facts: intended where noncombustible cladding is required
cone calorimeter data and flame-spread rating 75

missing_info.field: specific building, limiting distance and opening percentage
missing_info.why: the required construction depends on the exposing building face

gold.departure: Combustible composite cladding on exposing building faces where the table requires noncombustible cladding, without the full-scale wall-assembly test.

should_cite.why: full-scale test acceptance criteria referenced by the Part 9 route

gold.engineering_reason: Depends on the building it goes on: buildings outside the Division C exemption need registered professionals.

authoring.author: Batatis evaluation builder (Claude Opus 5.5)
authoring.notes: Written from the code database only; held-out judge set not consulted.
